subject: botany
question_text: Define metabolism. What is the difference between anabolism and catabolism?

verification.note: Chapter 1 (The Living World) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Botany Fastrack, book p.3 (VSAQ 8 of 9), which prints the question, a model answer and a two-column anabolism/catabolism table, but no star ranks and no year citations (a handwritten margin note in the scanned copy adds the examples photosynthesis and respiration — they are the standard examples and the card includes them). Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this chapter; 'not checked' here means exactly that, never 'checked and clean'. The 1+1 mark split is a claim until a TS IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition of metabolism
lines: Metabolism is the sum total of all chemical
reactions occurring in the body of a living

lines.text: Metabolism = sum of all chemical reactions

steps.why: 'Sum total of all chemical reactions' is the phrase the examiner looks for — metabolism is not one reaction but the complete set going on in the body.
common_mistakes: Writing 'metabolism is digestion' or 'energy production'. It is ALL the chemical reactions in the body, taken together.
Leaving out 'chemical reactions'. Without those words the definition is incomplete.
steps.memory_tip: Metabolism is the total; anabolism and catabolism are its two halves.
steps.margin_note: One sentence with 'sum total of all chemical reactions' earns the mark.

steps.label: Anabolism vs catabolism
lines: molecules are built into complex molecules.
molecules are broken into simple molecules.
steps.why: The two halves of metabolism run in opposite directions: anabolism builds (simple to complex), catabolism breaks (complex to simple). Photosynthesis and respiration are the standard examples — the scanned book carries them as a handwritten margin note.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two terms. Anabolism builds up; catabolism breaks down.
Giving the directions without examples. One example each (photosynthesis, respiration) completes the contrast.
steps.memory_tip: Anabolism Adds up; Catabolism Cuts down — match the first letters.
steps.margin_note: Write the contrast as two matched lines — direction plus one example on each side.

insider_note: The definition must say 'sum total of all chemical reactions'; the contrast also earns full credit written as a small two-column table.
